Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits the ZINB model $$P(Y_i = 0) = \pi_i + (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta), \qquad P(Y_i = y) = (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(y;\mu_i,\theta),\ y \ge 1,$$ with \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) (count model) and \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\) (zero-inflation model), by an EM algorithm:

  • E-step: \(\tau_i = \pi_i / \{\pi_i + (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta)\}\) if \(y_i = 0\), else \(\tau_i = 0\).

  • M-step, zero part: logistic IRLS on the fractional response \(\tau_i\).

  • M-step, count part: the NB fit of nbreg() with prior weights \(a_i = 1 - \tau_i\).

Usage

zinbreg(formula, data, offset, control = zinbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before |, zero-model covariates after it. Without | the same covariates are used in both parts, as in pscl::zeroinfl(). Offsets (offset() terms) are allowed in the count part.

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

Optional offset for the count model, evaluated in data.

control

A list from zinbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "zinbreg", a list with components coefficients (a list with count and zero), vcov (for \((\beta,\gamma)\), named count_* and zero_* as in zeroinfl()), vcov_full (also including log(theta)), theta, SE.theta, SE.logtheta, loglik, iter, converged, monotone (did the log-likelihood never decrease?), fitted.values (\((1-\hat\pi)\hat\mu\)), mu, pi, tau, residuals (response), score (gradient at the estimate), trace, y, offset, nobs, df.residual, call, formula, terms, xlevels, contrasts and control.

Details

EM stops when the observed-data log-likelihood changes by less than control$tol; a warning is given if it ever decreases. Standard errors come from inverting the observed information of the observed-data log-likelihood in \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\).

See also

nbreg(), zinbreg-methods

Examples

# Simulated data: count part beta = (1, 0.5), zero part gamma = (-1, 1), theta = 2
set.seed(1)
n <- 500
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
structural_zero <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + d$z))
d$y <- ifelse(structural_zero == 1, 0, rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x)))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> zinbreg(formula = y ~ x | z, data = d)

#> Log(theta)   0.67132    0.19094   3.516 0.000438 ***
#> ---
